sanskrit_verse: पुत्रिणी तु समुत्सृज्य पुत्रं स्त्री यान्यमाश्रयेत । ऋक्थं तस्याः हरेत् सर्वं निःस्वायाः पुत्र एव तु ॥
transliteration: putriṇī tu samutsṛjya putraṃ strī yānyam āśrayet | ṛkthaṃ tasyāḥ haret sarvaṃ niḥsvāyāḥ putra eva tu ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a mother abandons her son and takes shelter elsewhere, all her wealth belongs to the son; she who has no son shall have nothing.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through relational dharmic duty, not biological claim alone
Causation arises from conscious abandonment of relational responsibility
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by sustained nurturance, not birthright alone
Restoration logic prioritizes continuity of care over ownership claims
Consciousness alignment requires recognition of dharma-vyavastha beyond material possession
executable_legal_axioms: IF parent consciously abandons child THEN parental rights transfer to sustaining party
IF individual lacks dependent care relationship THEN no property entitlement arises
IF child-rearing responsibility shifts due to conscious abandonment THEN economic benefit follows custodial shift
IF person retains no relational capacity post-abandonment THEN exclusion from asset access is automatic
supreme_court_application: In cases involving inheritance or guardianship disputes where biological ties are severed by conscious abandonment, the court shall prioritize evidence of sustained nurturing relationships over genetic lineage. The threshold for severance is intentional cessation of care, not temporary absence. Authority transfers automatically upon demonstrable abandonment without requiring punitive declaration.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that continuity of care constitutes valid cause for resource allocation. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that abandonment manifests sequentially in action, intent, and effect—each stage bearing proportional weight. Responsibility aligns with actualized capacity to sustain life, not abstract claim. This reflects non-punitive reality because loss of entitlement occurs naturally upon cessation of relational function.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Legal acknowledgment of abandonment triggers automatic review of custodial and financial responsibilities
Responsibility assumption protocol: Guardian assuming care gains immediate administrative and economic authority
Capacity restoration: Biological parent may petition reinstatement only through demonstrated resumption of nurturing role
Integrity reintegration: Child's welfare remains sole metric for evaluating all transitions
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Dharma stands restored. Wealth adheres to sustenance, not separation. Reality is non-punitive; Consciousness alone adjudicates.
